description: Use the actual four-node early-Advance prefix established by exploration cfa40e9c46064645aa6322f0a0286660, then independently compare request-specific pre-commit queue membership after configuration-driven first current-term commitment. Finish all work and record later completion of that same request.

harness.description: TestAssuranceReadGateRelease uses real RawNodes and MemoryStorage with caller-owned deterministic network/application scheduling. Per-context queue membership is observed, never assigned.
semantic_changes: Only a package-local test is added; target protocol and dependencies are unchanged.
MemoryStorage and deterministic caller worker/network scheduling replace an unspecified deployment backend under a no-crash scope.
The explicit early-Advance optimization is selected: one committed configuration is persisted/advanced before its ApplyConfChange; later application is kept in order.
Unexported protocol state is read for observations and setup checks, with no direct critical-state writes.
Normal commands are no-op application payloads; Ready read results are recorded, not interpreted as a client state-machine reply.

legality.derivation: Four actual RawNodes bootstrap the same voters, persist/apply initial entries, and elect node 1. A real ProposeConfChange removes node 4. Node 2 persists its committed removal entry and advances the Ready while deferring only its actual ApplyConfChange. Other nodes apply normally. The explicit early-Advance permission in S_early_advance_usage and S_node_advance_order is used through RawNode's S_api correspondence to Node; the contrary shorthand in S_raw_advance_contract is retained. No subsequent entry is applied before the deferred configuration; the driver fails if that ordering would occur. A real Campaign on node 2 gets authentic votes including node 4, which node 2 still regards as a voter. Only node 2 and 3 acknowledge its new-term entry; under its still-active four-voter configuration that is not a quorum. After ReadIndex has been retained, actual ApplyConfChange reduces the voter set to three and consumes the retained Match values, permitting first current-term commitment.
legality.applicability: Synchronous Ready/Advance mode, ReadOnlySafe default, fresh unique request contexts, serialized calls and no crash. Storage is actual MemoryStorage; writes remain available for the whole no-crash execution, without a disk durability claim. All network messages come from Ready; delayed messages to/from the old leader and current-term appends to node 4 are later delivered unchanged. The recently removed node 4 is kept alive to answer actual requests from node 2's still-active old configuration; vote granting is source-defined and not stubbed. Every Ready persists entries/HardState before messages and Advance. Delayed configuration application is completed before any later committed entry application. No direct term/log/progress/commit assignment is performed. After activation, all queued messages are delivered, three leader ticks and a fresh read are processed, then an independent proposal permits the old request to complete. These finite steps terminate independently of the gate being checked and impose no deadline.
unresolved: Semantic review must judge the early-Advance interpretation and narrow internal queue expectation; no claim of general read liveness follows from execution.
conflicts: RawNode.Advance describes applied-and-saved completion. The check adopts the explicit Node/package early-Advance optimization; if a stricter configuration-specific ordering is required, this prefix is excluded.
alternatives: Applying the removal before Advance makes the campaign guard see the active configuration sooner and changes this prefix.
Fresh read retry may succeed under the public lossy API while the old retained request remains gated; retry success is a control, not the property.

grounding.derivation: C_read_gate_release concerns the pre-commit queue, not guaranteed public completion. The driver searches pendingReadIndexMessages for the exact fresh context (waiting-before-config) and observes membership after the actual configuration call, all emitted Ready/network work, three heartbeat rounds and one independently completed fresh request. The antecedent is independently established by retained (specific request present, current-term commit false) followed by activated (current-term commit true, same leader term). Operation/node/request_context are stable identifiers; pending_request is only the compared value and is never a result applicability filter. The assertion pending_request == false checks whether the old request remains specifically behind the now-satisfied current-term prerequisite. The result commit and term must match activation, excluding a hidden later commitment or leader change. Later-proposal completion of the same request is recorded after the measured result and does not admit or filter it.
grounding.applicability: One designated retained request, one membership activation, and one measured gate endpoint per stream. The admission alias activated represents the completed prerequisite-changing transition whose gate effect is owed. The later direct read and proposal controls are actual calls, with Ready.ReadStates observed by context. The checker does not require every ReadIndex to return; it measures retention in the prerequisite-specific queue after this transition. Source has no independent timer/worker that moves requests out of this queue; its only release caller is acknowledgment-driven commit. Finite heartbeat rounds are diagnostic controls, not a liveness timeout.
unresolved: Whether the public early-Advance optimization extends to deferred ApplyConfChange remains explicit in the accepted scope.
alternatives: Clearing/dropping the retained message would not produce this violation: the oracle only rejects remaining in the pre-commit gate.
A separate asynchronous normal read protocol can take longer to produce a result; the oracle does not require immediate ReadState.

observable_properties.description: The retained request must no longer be in the first-current-term-commit waiting queue after that prerequisite is established and the emitted work is processed, without requiring an additional log commitment.

uncertainties: This is a documented internal queue-transition requirement, not an unconditional public ReadIndex completion guarantee.
Applicability includes the explicit synchronous early-Advance interpretation; RawNode shorthand and general loss allowance remain visible for review.
No time bound, stale-read result, crash scenario or deployment performance claim is checked.
The later proposal control is an attributed diagnostic endpoint for the same request, not part of admission or the oracle.
